To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the glycosaminoglycan chains are attached to the core protein via the serine residue of a serine-glycine disaccharide sequence, that the core protein is a glycoprotein with a molecular weight of 35 000, and that the core protein has two sites of attachment for glycosaminogycan chains.
1. The core structure of the glycoprotein, which has been termed the 'core protein', is the most important structural determinant of the carbohydrate chains.

the core protein of the proteoglycan is linked to the hyaluronate through the action of a specific glycosyltransferase that uses UDP-N-acetylglucosamine as the glycosyl donor and that the core protein is also glycosylated by a number of specific glycosyl-transferases that use UDP-GlcNAc, GDP-Man, UDP-Gal, and UDP-Xyl as the glycosyI donor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the structural and functional aspects of proteoglycans in connective tissue.
the structure and biosynthesis of the carbohydrate chains of proteoglycans.
the structure and function of glycoproteins in the cell membrane and extracellular matrix.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the glycosaminoglycan chains of the proteoglycans of arterial tissue are highly heterogeneous and that the structure of the glycosaminolycans of each of these proteoglycants is different.
the interaction of proteoglycan with protein is complex and not well understood.

the glycosaminoglycan chains of proteoglycans are covalently bound to core proteins by O-glycosidic linkages to serine or threonine residues, and that the linkage region is a trisaccharide, Gal(1-3)GalNAc(1-4)Ser or Thr.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the glycosaminoglycans are not randomly attached to the core proteins but are organized in a defined pattern.
the structure of the carbohydrate chains of glycoproteins and proteoglycans is not random.
we have shown that the carbohydrate moieties of the core proteins are extensively modified in the extracellular matrix.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the protein core of the glycosaminoglycans (GAGs) is a major factor in determining their structure.
there are many more proteins than we thought that are modified by glycosaminoglycans.
there is a very strong relationship between the amount of protein and the amount of proteoglycans in the arterial wall.
